# Signature test vectors (test-only keys)

Independent vectors for the signature verification implemented in this
package (`lib/src/internal/crypto`). **Every key in this directory is a
test-only key, including the private keys in `signing_keys.json`. Never
configure any of them anywhere a real token could be accepted.**

The vectors were produced once by a small throwaway Go program (Go 1.27.1,
standard library only: `crypto/rsa`, `crypto/ecdsa`, `crypto/elliptic`,
`crypto/ed25519`, `crypto/sha256`, `crypto/sha1`). The `valid` expectation of
every case was decided by Go's own verifier, never by the Dart code under
test (the exceptions are listed below). They are committed as data and are
not regenerated by the test suite.

| File | Contents | Oracle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rs256.json` | RS256 with 2048, 3072 and 4096-bit keys: valid signatures over four messages, and tampered message or signature, unrelated key, signature one byte short or long, empty signature, representative equal to n, SHA-1 DigestInfo, DigestInfo without NULL, block type 02, shortened padding with trailing data, hash without DigestInfo, PSS signature presented as RS256; plus keys that must be skipped (1024 bits, even modulus, e = 1, no modulus) | `rsa.VerifyPKCS1v15` |
| `ps256.json` | PS256 with 2048, 2049 (EM one byte shorter than the modulus), 3072 and 4096-bit keys: valid signatures, tampering, unrelated key, wrong lengths, representative equal to n, salt lengths 0 and 64, PKCS#1 v1.5 signature presented as PS256, hand-built encodings (valid, MGF1-SHA-1, trailer 0xbb, top bits not cleared) | `rsa.VerifyPSS` with `SaltLength: PSSSaltLengthEqualsHash` (RFC 7518 section 3.5) |
| `es256.json` | ES256 (JWS `r \|\| s`) with two P-256 keys: valid signatures, high-S (valid), tampered message, r or s, unrelated key, swapped r and s, r or s equal to 0 or n, r + n, all-zero, 63 and 65-byte signatures, a DER signature, empty; plus keys that must be skipped (point off the curve, x not reduced, short and long coordinates, P-384, x = p) | `ecdsa.Verify` (only 64-byte signatures can be valid) |
| `ed25519.json` | EdDSA: RFC 8032 section 7.1 tests 1 to 3 (with their seeds, so the test signer can reproduce them), generated signatures, S + L and S = L (non-canonical S), S with the top bits set, tampered message, R or S, unrelated key, wrong lengths, all-zero, R with y = p, R off the curve, public keys with y = p or off the curve; plus keys that must be skipped (31 bytes, Ed448, X25519) | `ed25519.Verify`, except `r_non_canonical_y` and `public_key_non_canonical`, which are invalid because RFC 8032 point decoding rejects y >= p |
| `jwt.json` | Complete ES256 and PS256 access tokens signed by Go, with the key set and verification time: valid tokens (2048 and 4096-bit PS256), another key under the same kid, a DER signature, PSS salt length 0, a header algorithm that differs from the JWK's, a tampered payload | expected `VerifierErrorCode` values |
| `signing_keys.json` | Three test-only RSA private keys (JWK with CRT parameters) for the test signer in `test/support/signer.dart`, which mints tokens at test time like the Node.js tests do with `node:crypto`. EC and Ed25519 test keys are generated per run | none (input only) |

In the signature files, `keys` maps a kid to a public JWK, `cases[]` has
`name`, `kid`, `msg` (hex), `sig` (hex), `valid` and `why`, and
`invalid_keys[]` lists JWKs that `importJwk` must skip.
`test/crypto_vectors_test.dart` runs all of them;
`test/verifier_test.dart` runs `jwt.json`.

The shared access-token fixtures in `sdk/fixtures/access-tokens` (RS256 and
EdDSA, shared with the Go and Node.js SDKs) are run by
`test/fixtures_test.dart` and are not copied here.
